experiment.hypothesis: Building on a CoreRank cross-domain mechanism bridge between ProbMoE's calibrated marginal subset routing and BatchTopK Sparse Autoencoders, we diagnose why naive full-backward probabilistic replacement degrades reconstruction fidelity (active-set gradient magnitude distortion) and propose MarginProb-BatchTopK: preserving exact straight-through gradients on active top-k latents while routing scale-invariant calibrated marginal surrogate gradients exclusively to near-margin inactive latents. We benchmark 9 SAE architectures at 4x overcompleteness (d_sae=8,192) across two open-weight LLM families (Qwen3-1.7B L13 and SmolLM2-1.7B L12), three sparsity levels (k in {16, 32, 64}), three random seeds, and ~180,000 leak-free real tokens.

analysis.abstract_text: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) trained with hard TopK or BatchTopK activations rely on straight-through estimators (STE) that route zero gradient to inactive dictionary atoms, driving severe dead-latent collapse at high expansion factors (up to 78.6% dead atoms at 4x overcompleteness). Inspired by a CoreRank cross-domain bridge linking ProbMoE's differentiable marginal subset routing to BatchTopK SAEs, we first diagnose why naive full-backward probabilistic replacement (ProbBatchTopK v1) degrades reconstruction fidelity: multiplying active top-k gradients by sigmoid derivatives distorts feature magnitudes. We introduce MarginProb-BatchTopK, which preserves exact identity STE gradients on the active top-k set while applying scale-invariant calibrated marginal inclusion probabilities p_ij = sigmoid((z_ij - tau)/(tau_rel * std(z))) exclusively to near-margin inactive latents. We benchmark 9 L0-matched SAE architectures at 4x overcompleteness (d_in=2,048 -> d_sae=8,192) across two distinct open-weight LLM families (Qwen3-1.7B L13 and SmolLM2-1.7B L12; 205,883 real tokens with strict paper-level train/test splits), three sparsity levels (k in {16, 32, 64}), and 3 random seeds (162 main runs plus 24 ablation runs). Across all 18 paired runs, active-set gating completely eliminates v1's FVU penalty (delta FVU = -0.01569, 95% CI [-0.01837, -0.01301], paired t p=1.95e-09). Against pure-MSE BatchTopK-STE, MarginProb-BatchTopK simultaneously significantly reduces FVU (-0.00470, p=4.10e-03) and slashes dead latents by -19.90 percentage points (p=7.69e-09) with ZERO auxiliary loss. At k=32, pure-MSE MarginProb-BatchTopK beats even published SOTA BatchTopK+AuxK on both models (Qwen3 FVU 0.2796 vs. 0.2806, dead 20.1% vs. 31.1%; SmolLM2 FVU 0.2720 vs. 0.2729, probe recovery 108.6%), and at k=64 reduces dead latents 3x-8x below BatchTopK+AuxK (1.53% vs. 12.17% on Qwen3; 5.16% vs. 15.61% on SmolLM2). Sweeping lambda in [0, 0.60] smoothly controls dead latents from 55.8% down to 1.32% with an FVU optimum at lambda=0.05 (0.2786).
findings: Active-set gating completely eliminates v1's FVU penalty across 18 paired 4x-overcomplete runs (2 LLM families x 3 k x 3 seeds): MarginProb-BatchTopK lowers FVU vs. ungated v1 ProbBatchTopK by -0.01569 (95% CI [-0.01837, -0.01301], paired t p=1.95e-09; Qwen3 k=32: 0.2996 -> 0.2796; SmolLM2 k=32: 0.2826 -> 0.2720).

Pure-MSE MarginProb-BatchTopK strictly Pareto-dominates BatchTopK-STE across 18 paired runs with zero auxiliary loss: FVU delta = -0.00470 (p=4.10e-03, Wilcoxon p=3.36e-03) AND dead-latent reduction = -19.90 pp (95% CI [-23.62, -16.18], p=7.69e-09).

Surpassing published SOTA BatchTopK+AuxK at k=32 and k=64: At k=32, pure-MSE MarginProb-BatchTopK beats BatchTopK+AuxK on FVU on both models (Qwen3 0.2796 vs. 0.2806, dead 20.1% vs. 31.1%; SmolLM2 0.2720 vs. 0.2729, highest 8-class probe recovery 108.6%). At k=64, dead latents drop 8x on Qwen3 (1.53% vs. 12.17%) and 3x on SmolLM2 (5.16% vs. 15.61%); at ultra-sparse k=16, AuxK retains a modest dead-latent edge (51.0% vs. 58.5% on Qwen3), while TopK+AuxK stays strongest on pure FVU at k=16.

Smooth Pareto control via boundary weight lambda (Qwen3-1.7B, k=32, 3 seeds): Increasing lambda from 0.00 -> 0.05 -> 0.15 -> 0.30 -> 0.60 monotonically reduces dead latents from 55.8% -> 33.4% -> 20.1% -> 9.1% -> 1.32% (42x reduction) while lifting utilization entropy from 0.837 -> 0.918, achieving an FVU minimum at lambda=0.05 (0.2786).

analysis.fig_caption: Figure 1. 4x overcomplete SAE benchmark (d_sae = 8,192, 3 seeds) on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090. (a) Reconstruction FVU vs. dead-latent Pareto frontier across k in {16, 32, 64} on Qwen3-1.7B L13. (b) Cross-architecture FVU generalization (Qwen3-1.7B L13 vs. SmolLM2-1.7B L12 at k=32, 95% CIs). (c) Dead-latent collapse vs. downstream 8-class paper-category linear probe recovery at k=32. (d) Boundary surrogate weight λ ablation showing how active-set gating eliminates ungated v1's FVU penalty.
limitations: Straight-through margin gradients update W_enc and b_enc for near-margin inactive features without updating W_dec, so deeply dead latents still benefit from AuxK.
Evaluated at 4x overcompleteness (d_sae=8,192) over 205,883 leak-free tokens across two 1.7B models; 65k-131k production scale over 100M+ tokens warrants future study.
Downstream semantics are evaluated via 8-class category linear probe recovery rather than per-latent LLM auto-interpretability scoring.
